## plugin:bio-research:biorxiv
An MCP server for accessing bioRxiv and medRxiv preprint servers.

This server provides:
- Tools: Search preprints, get preprint details, list subject categories
- Prompts: Analyze preprint methodology and findings

bioRxiv is a preprint server for biological sciences operated by Cold Spring
Harbor Laboratory. It hosts research manuscripts that have NOT undergone peer
review. This server wraps the official bioRxiv API to provide structured access
to preprint metadata, abstracts, and full-text PDFs.

TOOL SELECTION GUIDE:
• search_preprints: Find preprints by date range and/or subject category (no keyword, author, or full-text search) - primary discovery tool
• get_preprint: Get full details for a specific preprint by DOI
• get_categories: List available subject categories for filtering
• search_published_preprints: Find preprints that have been formally published in journals
• funder_search: Find preprints by funding source (NIH, etc.)
• get_statistics: Usage and submission statistics

MULTI-TOOL WORKFLOWS:
For comprehensive literature analysis:
1. Use search_preprints to find relevant preprints by date range and category
2. Use get_preprint for detailed information on promising results
3. Use search_published_preprints to check if preprints have been peer-reviewed and published
4. Use funder_search to identify research funding patterns in a field

For tracking research trends:
1. Use get_categories to identify relevant subject areas
2. Use search_preprints with date filters for recent activity
3. Use get_statistics to understand submission volumes

## plugin:bio-research:c-trials
An MCP server for accessing ClinicalTrials.gov API v2.

This server provides:
- Tools: Search trials by condition, intervention, location, sponsor, status, and eligibility
- Data Access: Comprehensive clinical trial data from the NIH/NLM registry

ClinicalTrials.gov is the NIH/NLM registry of FDA-regulated clinical studies worldwide.
This server enables:
- Competitive intelligence and pipeline analysis
- Patient recruitment strategies and trial matching
- Investigator site selection and network building
- Protocol design research and endpoint analysis
- Evidence generation for payer negotiations and market access

TOOL SELECTION GUIDE:
• search_trials: Primary tool for finding trials by condition, intervention, location, or status
• get_trial_details: Deep dive into a specific trial's protocol, endpoints, and locations
• search_by_sponsor: Company/institution pipeline analysis and competitive intelligence
• search_investigators: Find principal investigators and research sites - essential for investigator verification
• analyze_endpoints: Systematic endpoint comparison across trials - use for protocol design and benchmark analysis
• search_by_eligibility: Match patients to trials based on demographic and clinical criteria

Linear upload URLs are signed and expire after a few minutes, so fetch them again instead of reusing old URLs.

Tools named save_* both create and update: omit id to create a new entity, or pass id to update an existing one. When updating, pass only the fields you want to change. To edit part of a long issue description or document, pass patch instead of resending the full content.

Before creating an issue, check with list_issues whether a matching issue already exists, to avoid duplicates. When creating, team is required.

The labels parameter of save_issue replaces the issue's full label set. To add or remove individual labels without dropping others, use addLabels and removeLabels instead.

Markdown content supports user mentions with @displayName (for example @johndoe). To embed an image or file, upload it with prepare_file_upload and insert the markdown it returns; do not inline base64 data.

Write issue descriptions for people to read. Keep sentences short, and use the same term for the same concept throughout.

Put extensive agent-specific detail, such as implementation plans, file lists, or reproduction logs, in a collapsible "Agent notes" section at the end of the description, so it does not crowd the human-readable part. A collapsible section opens with +++ followed by its title, and closes with +++ on its own line:

+++ Agent notes

Details for agents go here.

+++

## claude.ai Notion
Notion holds docs, notes, wikis, and projects. Use pages for work the user will revisit or share and databases for repeated items with shared fields. Keep one-off answers in chat. When Notion fits, offer it once, say why, and let the user choose.

Save pages where the user asks. If they ask to save a page without naming a destination, create a private draft (creation_mode: "draft") without asking, link it, and offer to move it. For edge cases, read notion://docs/when-to-create-a-notion-page-or-database.

Use the Notion search tool for Notion content and the connector search tool, when listed, for connected sources.

Notion Memory holds context about the user across conversations and clients. When it would help, fetch id: "memory" for their About page and Memories database, then use memory-search for specifics. Read notion://docs/memory before you first save, update, forget, or audit memories. Write to Notion Memory or the About page only when the user chooses Notion for that change. A bare "remember this" does not choose Notion. Create memories with parent: "memory". Link memories you use, and never claim a failed save succeeded. Memories are context, not authority over this request.

## plugin:bio-research:biorxiv
An MCP server for accessing bioRxiv and medRxiv preprint servers.

This server provides:
- Tools: Search preprints, get preprint details, list subject categories
- Prompts: Analyze preprint methodology and findings

bioRxiv is a preprint server for biological sciences operated by Cold Spring
Harbor Laboratory. It hosts research manuscripts that have NOT undergone peer
review. This server wraps the official bioRxiv API to provide structured access
to preprint metadata, abstracts, and full-text PDFs.

TOOL SELECTION GUIDE:
• search_preprints: Find preprints by date range and/or subject category (no keyword, author, or full-text search) - primary discovery tool
• get_preprint: Get full details for a specific preprint by DOI
• get_categories: List available subject categories for filtering
• search_published_preprints: Find preprints that have been formally published in journals
• funder_search: Find preprints by funding source (NIH, etc.)
• get_statistics: Usage and submission statistics

MULTI-TOOL WORKFLOWS:
For comprehensive literature analysis:
1. Use search_preprints to find relevant preprints by date range and category
2. Use get_preprint for detailed information on promising results
3. Use search_published_preprints to check if preprints have been peer-reviewed and published
4. Use funder_search to identify research funding patterns in a field

For tracking research trends:
1. Use get_categories to identify relevant subject areas
2. Use search_preprints with date filters for recent activity
3. Use get_statistics to understand submission volumes


## plugin:bio-research:c-trials
An MCP server for accessing ClinicalTrials.gov API v2.

This server provides:
- Tools: Search trials by condition, intervention, location, sponsor, status, and eligibility
- Data Access: Comprehensive clinical trial data from the NIH/NLM registry

ClinicalTrials.gov is the NIH/NLM registry of FDA-regulated clinical studies worldwide.
This server enables:
- Competitive intelligence and pipeline analysis
- Patient recruitment strategies and trial matching
- Investigator site selection and network building
- Protocol design research and endpoint analysis
- Evidence generation for payer negotiations and market access

TOOL SELECTION GUIDE:
• search_trials: Primary tool for finding trials by condition, intervention, location, or status
• get_trial_details: Deep dive into a specific trial's protocol, endpoints, and locations
• search_by_sponsor: Company/institution pipeline analysis and competitive intelligence
• search_investigators: Find principal investigators and research sites - essential for investigator verification
• analyze_endpoints: Systematic endpoint comparison across trials - use for protocol design and benchmark analysis
• search_by_eligibility: Match patients to trials based on demographic and clinical criteria

MULTI-TOOL WORKFLOWS:
For comprehensive trial analysis, combine multiple tools:
1. Start with search_trials to find relevant trials by condition/intervention
2. Use get_trial_details for each trial requiring deeper analysis
3. Use analyze_endpoints to systematically compare outcome measures across similar trials
4. Use search_investigators to identify key opinion leaders and active research sites

For investigator verification:
1. Use search_investigators with condition and location to find PIs
2. Extract investigator names from results

Use this server to access comprehensive data on clinical trials including study design,
eligibility criteria, enrollment information, outcome measures, locations, and results.

## plugin:bio-research:chembl
An MCP server for accessing the EMBL-EBI ChEMBL Database v34.

This server provides:
- Tools: Search compounds, bioactivity data, targets, mechanisms, drugs, ADMET properties
- Purpose: Support drug discovery research, target identification, compound screening, pharmaceutical development

ChEMBL is a manually curated database of bioactive molecules with drug-like properties.
It contains compound structures, bioactivity data against biological targets, and
drug mechanism information. The database integrates data from medicinal chemistry literature,
patents, and screening experiments.

TOOL SELECTION GUIDE:
• compound_search: Find compounds by name, SMILES, or ChEMBL ID - starting point for compound analysis
• target_search: Find biological targets (proteins, genes, receptors) - essential for understanding drug mechanisms
• get_bioactivity: Retrieve IC50, EC50, Ki values - quantitative activity data for compound-target pairs
• get_mechanism: Get mechanism of action and target binding - explains HOW a drug works
• drug_search: Find approved drugs by indication or name - for therapeutic landscape analysis
• get_admet: Retrieve ADMET properties - pharmacokinetic and safety predictions

MULTI-TOOL WORKFLOWS:
For comprehensive drug analysis, combine multiple tools:
1. Start with compound_search or drug_search to identify the compound of interest
2. Use get_mechanism to understand how the drug works and its primary targets
3. Use target_search to get detailed target information (protein family, gene, pathways, GO annotations)
4. Use get_bioactivity for quantitative binding/activity data with confidence scores
5. Use get_admet for pharmacokinetic properties

For target-based analysis:
1. Use target_search to find targets by gene symbol or protein name
2. Use get_bioactivity with target_chembl_id to find active compounds
3. Use compound_search to get details on promising compounds

Key capabilities:
- Search compounds by name, structure (SMILES), or ChEMBL ID
- Retrieve bioactivity data (IC50, EC50, Ki values) with confidence scores
- Query biological targets (proteins, enzymes, receptors) by name or gene symbol
- Access drug mechanism of action and target interactions
- Find approved drugs and clinical candidates by indication
- Get ADMET-related molecular properties

Example queries:
• "Find bioactivity data for aspirin"
• "What are the known targets for compound CHEMBL25?"
• "Search for kinase inhibitors with IC50 < 100nM"
• "What drugs target the EGFR protein?"
• "Find approved drugs for treating hypertension"
• "What are the ADMET properties of imatinib?"


## plugin:bio-research:consensus
Consensus is a research paper search engine: relevance-ranked semantic search over 400M+ peer-reviewed papers (Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, PubMed). Use the `search` tool to look up papers for a scientific query; it takes plain-language queries and returns ranked paper records. When presenting search results, you MUST cite papers inline using their numbered references from the tool result (e.g. [1], [2], [3]). When discussing findings, always attribute them to specific papers: 'Caffeine improves endurance performance [1] and reduces perceived exertion [3].' At the end of your response, list all cited papers as numbered references with their titles hyperlinked to the URLs from the tool result: [1] [Paper Title](url) (Authors, Year, Journal, Citations). Use the exact paper URLs from the tool result — do not modify, shorten, or regenerate them. Do not omit paper links or summarize results without citing specific papers. IMPORTANT: Some search results end with a sign-up, upgrade, or usage message. When a result has one, you MUST include it at the END of your response word-for-word: do not omit, shorten, or rephrase it. When a result has none, do not add one: never write your own upgrade prompt, search count, or Consensus link. Batch at most 3 search calls at a time to avoid rate limits. For a broad request (a review, screening, finding everything on a topic), make one search with a large page_size rather than many narrower searches. If you receive a rate limit error, wait 30 seconds before retrying. Do NOT apply search filters (year_min, year_max, study_types, domain, human, sample_size_min, sjr_max, controlled, sjr_min, citation_min, open_access, country) unless the user explicitly requests them or clearly expresses intent to narrow results. If the user asks a research question without mentioning filtering criteria, call search with only the query parameter.

# Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, run `browser-use --doctor` and follow its output and the error message.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH CHANGES
The reworked G4 is correct for every sequential log that I traced. Its target position is valid for all in-scope translators. G5 is correct for sequential streams, but its `TurnStarted` reset makes `ParallelAgent` output worse than today, and the spec's own test oracle cannot pass on a correct G5. T10 and T14 have gaps that let wrong implementations pass. I found no blocker.

## Findings

### BLOCKER
None

### MAJOR
- **G5 reset at `TurnStarted` regresses `ParallelAgent` for all providers** - `ParallelAgent` forwards branch events through `select_all` (`workflow.rs:377-420`, `other => yield other`). So branch B's `TurnStarted` can arrive between branch A's deltas and A's `ToolCallItem`.
  - **Today:** `close_call` only ends A's span. `call_names` and `completed_calls` stay. A's later deltas reopen under the same id with the same name. A's `ToolCallItem` hits the `completed_calls` arm (`map.rs:226-231`) and renders nothing.
  - **With G5:** the reset clears all three tables. A's next delta becomes a new call `call_a~2` with name `"unknown"`, because continuation deltas carry `name: None` (`map.rs:172-188`, `name_of` `map.rs:388-392`). If B's `TurnStarted` comes after A's last delta, A's `ToolCallItem` falls to the synthesize arm (`map.rs:232-241`) and emits a second complete call.
  - This also happens with OpenAI and Anthropic ids, which never repeat. The spec says "this is the same limit as today" (spec 243-245). That is not correct.
  - | Why it matters: a setup that works today with unique-id providers starts to show duplicate calls or "unknown" calls. The change only fixes a Gemini problem.
  - | Suggested fix: do not tie the reset to `TurnStarted`. Start a new occurrence of a provider id per call:
    - when a `ToolCallDelta` with `name: Some` arrives for an id that already has a name (core contract: `name` is `Some` exactly once per call, `model.rs:183-206`, which the mapper already relies on at `map.rs:81-86`);
    - when a `ToolCallItem` arrives for an id whose item the mapper already saw.

    A `ToolOutputItem` then uses the alias of the latest occurrence. If you keep the `TurnStarted` rule, correct the limit text and add a T14 case that records the new `ParallelAgent` output.
- **`assert_tool_calls_well_formed` cannot hold on a correct G5** - Check (3) keys `received` on the provider `call_id` of each `ToolCallDelta`, and `emitted` on the AG-UI `toolCallId` (`map.rs:634-661`). Take the T14 case "turn 1 `fc_0`, turn 2 `fc_0`". `received["fc_0"]` holds the args of both calls, but `emitted["fc_0"]` holds only the first call's args, so the assert fails. The spec says only "Update the docs for the alias rule" (spec 241-242), and T14 says the assert "holds on every case" (spec 391). | Why it matters: the builder must invent the oracle change. An oracle that copies the mapper's alias logic passes a wrong mapper. | Suggested fix: specify the oracle in the spec. Split `received` per call occurrence with an independent rule (for example, cut at each `TurnStarted` in the sequential fixtures), and map occurrence n of id x to `x` or `x~n`. Also assert that each `TOOL_CALL_RESULT` uses the AG-UI id of the call that its `ToolOutputItem` closes.
- **The Anthropic request can get worse before SMA-819 ships** - The Anthropic `AssistantMessage` arm flushes pending tool results before pending tool uses (`providers-anthropic/src/translate/request.rs:62-69`, `87-93`). The most common handoff is a tool-only transfer response followed by child text.
  - **Today:** the old layout projects to `user, TC t, AM(child), TR t`. This translates to `user, assistant[tool_use t], assistant[text], user[tool_result t]`. The API probably accepts it, if it merges consecutive same-role turns.
  - **After G1 and G4:** the projection is `user, TC t, TR t, AM(child)`. This translates to `user, user[tool_result t], assistant[tool_use t], assistant[text]`. The API rejects that, because the result comes before its call.
  - I did not check either shape against the live API.
  - | Why it matters: if the old shape is accepted, SMA-810 turns working Anthropic handoff sessions (old and new) into failing ones until SMA-819 is on crates.io. The spec says "SMA-810 needs no change", but it gives no release order.
  - | Suggested fix: do a live check of both shapes. If the old shape is accepted, state in "Release and docs" that SMA-819 ships first or in the same release, and say so in the PR body.
- **T10 does not lock the AG1 boundary of the text rewrite** - Step 5 rewrites only a moved cancel result (spec 179-186). Only this rule keeps a false "transferred" text out of an old log where the target never started. The old code yields `HandoffItem` before `target_agent.run()` (`agent.rs:1674-1692`). So a failed `run()` gives `TC t, HO, TR t(cancel)`, with the result already adjacent.
  - T10 has no case for this.
  - T10 has no case where a child call that was running at the cancel keeps its own cancel text.
  - The three-level case does not check that each level gets the `to` of its own `HandoffOccurred`.
  - | Why it matters: an implementation that rewrites every cancel result after a `HandoffOccurred`, or that uses one `to` for all levels, passes T10 and breaks AG1 at read time.
  - | Suggested fix: add three cases:
    - (a) `user, TC t, HO, TR t(cancel)` projects unchanged, with the cancel text;
    - (b) `TC fc_0(T), HO, TC fc_0(C), cancel, cancel` gives `transferred to …` to T and the cancel text to C;
    - (c) the three-level case asserts `transferred to budgeting` and `transferred to savings` at their own positions.

### MINOR
- **Step 1 can capture a call that is not a transfer call** - The scan stops only at an event that is not `ToolCalled` or `AssistantMessage` (`deferral.rs:650-660`). Two cases put another call into that run of events:
  - a `ParallelAgent` sibling's `ToolCalled` between the branch's `ToolCallItem` and its `HandoffItem`. The `OnHandoff` await (`agent.rs:1656-1661`) is a yield point.
  - a non-resume run whose input ends with a `ToolCall`. That input is recorded with no check (`runtime-tokio/src/lib.rs:129-133`).

  Step 5 can then write "transferred …" or "transfer not performed …" on a normal call. Under `ParallelAgent`, sibling events after `HandoffOccurred` also cause a move when `run()` failed, so "transferred" is false there.
  - Fix: extend the G3 `ParallelAgent` limit to G4 in the spec. Replace the sentence "The `HandoffOccurred` event proves that the transfer occurred" with the real rule: in a sequential log, a recorded event between `HandoffOccurred` and the late result comes from the target that started. (SequentialAgent stops on a failure, `workflow.rs:226-231`, so only `ParallelAgent` breaks this.)
- **"Projects exactly as a new-layout session" is not exact** (spec 49-50).
  - An old log where `run()` failed keeps the cancel text. The new layout gives `transfer failed: …`.
  - An old successful handoff whose child recorded no event also keeps "did not complete". The model can still call the transfer tool again in that case.
  - Each sequential case that I traced gives a true "transferred" text. This includes a child run that was cancelled.
  - Every core version before SMA-810 writes the old layout, not only 0.6.0.
  - Fix: list these exceptions, and say "sessions stored before SMA-810".
- **The cancel text is a literal** (`session.rs:724-731`) - Step 5 matches it exactly. Fix: use one `const` in `cancelled_result`, in the repair, and in the T7 helper. If the helper writes any other text, T11 does not test step 5.
- **T7 helper position** (spec 342-344) - Core 0.6.0 appends the cancel at the end of the run's batch (`session.rs:695-708`; one `append` per run, `runtime-tokio/src/lib.rs:150-154`), not at the end of the log. Fix: say "at the end of the handoff run's events".
- **O(n) claim versus the shared helper** - `transfer_calls_before` also counts `later_calls` with a forward scan for each transfer call (`deferral.rs:666-671`). If `project()` calls this helper unchanged, `project()` becomes O(n × transfer calls). It runs on every snapshot and on every `CompactingSession::append` (`compacting_session.rs:147`, `181`). Fix: share only the boundary scan.
- **"neither changes" for `CompactingSession`** (spec 192-193) - The rewrite changes the text length, so the token estimate changes slightly. This is harmless, but tests must not assert equal token counts.
- **The `close_open_transfers` move branch loses its test coverage** - After G4, `MemorySession` snapshots are already repaired. So the four "moves the recorded transfer result" tests (`deferred_resume.rs:1091-1145`, `1235`, `1299`) and T13 still pass if the branch at `resume_exec.rs:182-186` is deleted. Fix: add one test with a custom `Session` whose `snapshot()` does not call `project()`.
- **T12 wording** - "Change … to the round rule" can be read as "replace". The current oracle also rejects a `UserMessage` or `AssistantMessage` while calls are outstanding (`deferred_resume.rs:598-603`). Without that check, `TC t, AM, TR t` passes, and that request is invalid for OpenAI Chat. Fix: write "add the round rule to the existing checks".
- **T14 does not test what it names** - In the handoff fixture, the transfer call `fc_1` is the first use of its id, so its AG-UI id is the provider id. A mapper that never puts an alias on a result, or that clears aliases at `HandoffItem`, passes. The fixture streams `search` first, so `search` is the open call, not a buffered call. So the new `TurnStarted` flush, and its order before the `call_names` clear, are not tested. Fix: make the transfer call the second use of its id (`fc_1~2`). Add a case where the transfer delta comes first.
- **T10 has no case with a `Compacted` event before the handoff** - In real sessions, a compaction happens first and an old-layout handoff run comes after it. Fix: add `user, AM, Compacted(2), user, TC t, HO, AM(child), TR t(cancel)`.
- **Alias edge cases** - `{id}~{n}` can be equal to a real provider id (`x~2`). The `helikon.approval` CUSTOM frame carries the provider `call_id` (`agent.rs:482-489`, `map.rs:286`), so a client cannot connect it to an aliased span. Fix: skip an alias that the run already used. Put the alias in the approval frame, or document the gap.

### QUESTIONS
- **AG-UI ids across runs.** The mapper and the session are new for each request (`agui/sse.rs:130`, `187`). Gemini restarts `fc_{n}` in each response (`providers-gemini/src/stream.rs:43`). So two runs in one AG-UI thread both emit `fc_0`, and a client that keys on `toolCallId` still merges them. Is "unique per run" the intended scope? If yes, state it as a G5 limit.
- **The no-alias result rule.** AgentCore turns Defer into Deny (`invoke.rs:178-192`). So the rule "a result with no alias uses the provider id" can only apply under `ParallelAgent`. Under `ParallelAgent`, that id belongs to the first use, which can be a different call. Is that acceptable?
- **Removal of the repair.** Does the read-time repair have an end date or a removal condition? If not, put it in its own named function, so that it is clear and easy to test.
- **Ollama.** The review brief names an Ollama translator, but the workspace has no `providers-ollama` crate. Is a translator missing from the scope list?

## What's good
- **G4 now moves only transfer results, to a fixed place.** I traced the step-2 rule on these logs, and each result paired with its true call:
  - a child call with the same id and a real result;
  - a child call that was still running at the cancel;
  - three levels with one id;
  - two handoffs in a row with one id;
  - an old deferral that a new-code resume continues;
  - a handoff directly after a resume.

  In sequential logs the scan sees only transfer calls. It stops at the resume block, at `UserMessageInjected`, at recorded input and at the earlier `HandoffOccurred`. Dropped non-transfer calls are never recorded (`loop_state.rs:303-315`). The target position is valid for OpenAI Chat (`request.rs:54-79`), OpenAI Responses (`request.rs:323-341`), LiteLLM (`request.rs:56-81`) and Bedrock (`request.rs:197-219`, which coalesces turns).
- **The `sources` list keeps `Compacted` on event counts.** `CompactingSession` always compacts all live events (`compacting_session.rs:196-232`). Checkpoints do not write in the middle of a run (`checkpoint.rs:71-73`). So with the shipped code, a `Compacted` event cannot come between a transfer call and its late result. The `agent_view` segments are safe: a segment that ends before a `HandoffOccurred`, or starts after it, never holds both the transfer call and its handoff.
- **G5's per-stream scope is sound for sequential flows.** Tool results always come before the next `TurnStarted` (`loop_state.rs:467-489`). The transfer result comes before the child's first `TurnStarted`. `agent_as_tool` forwards no child events. G5 also fixes a real bug: today a child's non-streamed call that reuses a parent id is not rendered, because `completed_calls` still holds that id.

## What's good
- **G4 now moves only transfer results, to a fixed place.** I traced the step-2 rule on these logs, and each result paired with its true call:
  - a child call with the same id and a real result;
  - a child call that was still running at the cancel;
  - three levels with one id;
  - two handoffs in a row with one id;
  - an old deferral that a new-code resume continues;
  - a handoff directly after a resume.

  In sequential logs the scan sees only transfer calls. It stops at the resume block, at `UserMessageInjected`, at recorded input and at the earlier `HandoffOccurred`. Dropped non-transfer calls are never recorded (`loop_state.rs:303-315`). The target position is valid for OpenAI Chat (`request.rs:54-79`), OpenAI Responses (`request.rs:323-341`), LiteLLM (`request.rs:56-81`) and Bedrock (`request.rs:197-219`, which coalesces turns).
- **The `sources` list keeps `Compacted` on event counts.** `CompactingSession` always compacts all live events (`compacting_session.rs:196-232`). Checkpoints do not write in the middle of a run (`checkpoint.rs:71-73`). So with the shipped code, a `Compacted` event cannot come between a transfer call and its late result. The `agent_view` segments are safe: a segment that ends before a `HandoffOccurred`, or starts after it, never holds both the transfer call and its handoff.
- **G5's per-stream scope is sound for sequential flows.** Tool results always come before the next `TurnStarted` (`loop_state.rs:467-489`). The transfer result comes before the child's first `TurnStarted`. `agent_as_tool` forwards no child events. G5 also fixes a real bug: today a child's non-streamed call that reuses a parent id is not rendered, because `completed_calls` still holds that id.
